item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q005_cupredoxin_function_transfer","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, all three are all-beta proteins in the Cupredoxin-like fold b.6 (SUNID 49502) and, more specifically, the Cupredoxins superfamily b.6.1 (SUNID 49503). They are nevertheless separate families: Plastocyanin/azurin-like b.6.1.1 (SUNID 49504), Ephrin ectodomain b.6.1.5 (SUNID 74874), and the PAD4 N-terminal domain b.6.1.6 (SUNID 110107). Thus SCOPe asserts a probable distant evolutionary relationship at superfamily strength, not close family-level equivalence or shared biological function. Copper binding and electron transfer must not be transferred from plastocyanin/azurin-like proteins to ephrin ectodomains or PAD4's N-terminal domain. A member of b.6.1.1 is also not automatically copper-binding solely from its family label. Cross-family structures may serve as cautious fold-level templates, but not as functional representatives or templates for ligand placement. Target-specific evidence would be required: conservation and geometry of the complete copper-coordinating site, experimentally supported metal occupancy or spectroscopy, and direct redox/electron-transfer assays; structural resemblance or superfamily membership alone is insufficient.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope__get_scop_service_info — /api/v1/releases/current","mcp__scope__search_scop — /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=Plastocyanin&mode=auto&limit=20; /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=ephrin&mode=auto&limit=20; /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=PAD4&mode=auto&limit=20; /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=cupredoxin&mode=auto&limit=20","mcp__scope__get_scop_node — /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/b.6; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/b.6/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/b.6.1; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/b.6.1/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/b.6.1.1/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/b.6.1.5/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/b.6.1.6/parents"]}]}
